mission: Survivor displacement — the three confront the modern galaxy's changes. The Jedi Order restructured, the Republic transformed, everything they fought for either succeeded or was rewritten. Emotional cost of waking up in a future that doesn't remember you.
why_now: Before they can function as a team, they need to grieve what they've lost — and Ben needs to see them as people, not assets
conflict: Each survivor processes the displacement differently: Sera with rigid focus on the mission (avoiding grief), Torin with genuine curiosity and apparent adaptation (too easy), Kael with sardonic detachment
turning_point: Kael asks what happened to the Sith world he was taken from. Ben doesn't know. Nobody knows. It was too small to be in the records that survived. Kael's expression doesn't change, but something behind it does.
opening_hook: Sera asks about the Ruusan Reformations — what the galaxy was told they were for. Ben answers honestly. She goes very still.
closing_hook: Torin catches Ben's eye across the common area and nods — the nod of a commander acknowledging a subordinate who handled something difficult well. Ben isn't sure if he should be reassured or concerned that Torin is already thinking in command structure.
emotional_trajectory: Awkward information exchange -> raw grief (Kael's moment) -> fragile group empathy

stakes.personal: Ben seeing the human cost of what was done to these people
stakes.interpersonal: Building real connection vs. mission-focused alliance
stakes.external: The survivors' displacement is also an intelligence gap — they don't understand the modern galaxy's politics

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — common area, cramped and intimate
sensory_details: Desh's food supplies — modern field rations that taste different from anything the survivors know; the datapad with galactic history scrolling; Kael's silence filling the small space
promises_planted: Kael's detachment is a defense mechanism (PP09)
notes: Kael's moment about his homeworld is small but crucial — plants his arc. He's not detached because he doesn't care; he's detached because caring cost him everything and nobody ever asked.
